4 5 # televibe 6 7 A [Teleport](https://goteleport.com) access-request plugin that routes each pending request through an AI risk analyst, auto-approves the boring ones, and files an ITSM Jira ticket for the sketchy ones — with the Teleport request held in `PENDING` until an SRE resolves the ticket. 8 9 Risk tiers: 10 11 | Score | Tier | Action | 12 | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------- | 13 | 0–24 | low | auto-approve, no Jira ticket | 14 | 25–49 | medium | file ITSM ticket, hold request pending | 15 | 50–74 | high | file ITSM ticket with tier label | 16 | 75–100 | critical | file ITSM ticket with tier label | 17 18 The ticket-creation threshold is configurable (`risk.ticket_threshold`). Session escalations — access requests carrying the `televibe.escalation` Teleport annotation — use a tighter fallback threshold (`risk.escalation_threshold`) and support per-role overrides in `risk.escalation_thresholds`. 19 20 ## How it works 21 22 ``` 23 Teleport ──► watcher ──► scorer ──► AI provider ──► tier 24 │ 25 ├── below threshold ──► auto-approve via AccessReview 26 │ 27 └── at/above threshold ──► Jira ITSM ticket ──► poll status 28 │ 29 SRE approves/rejects │ 30 ▼ 31 Teleport AccessReview 32 ``` 33 34 **Risk components:** 35 36 - **Structural (deterministic):** missing `CUSTX-###` ticket reference (+30), thin description `<40` chars (+15), off-hours request (+10). 37 - **AI-judged (clamped):** description quality 0–25, privilege concern 0–25, anomalies 0–10. 38 39 ## User reputation 40 41 Every requester starts at `reputation.starting_score` (default `100`) and 42 accumulates deductions for each bad request they file. Penalties and the 43 `[floor, ceiling]` clamp are fully configurable: 44 45 | Signal | Config key | Default | 46 | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------- | 47 | Missing CUSTX ticket | `reputation.penalty_missing_custx` | `10` | 48 | Thin (<40 char) reason | `reputation.penalty_thin_description` | `5` | 49 50 State is persisted as a JSON map at `reputation.persist_path` via atomic 51 rename — no external database required. The file survives restarts; leave 52 `persist_path` empty to keep everything in memory. 53 54 Reputation only ever goes down. If somebody wants their number back, 55 they can file better requests next quarter. Or not. 56 57 ## Telemetry / shaming pipeline 58 59 When `telemetry.enabled = true`, televibe stands up an OpenTelemetry 60 `MeterProvider` with an OTLP/gRPC exporter pointed at the configured 61 collector. It registers one observable gauge: 62 63 - `televibe.user.reputation` — int64, tagged with `user`, observed every 64 `telemetry.export_period` (default `15s`). 65 66 Route your collector's output to Datadog (or Prometheus, or wherever) and 67 the gauge lands tagged per user, ready to be pinned to a dashboard for 68 the monthly team meeting. 69 70 ## AI providers 71 72 Pick one via `ai.provider`: 73 74 - **`anthropic`** — direct call to the Anthropic Messages API. System prompt is sent with `cache_control: ephemeral` so repeated scoring hits the prompt cache. 75 - **`bedrock`** — `bedrockruntime:InvokeModel` against a Claude-on-Bedrock model. Uses the default AWS credential chain (IRSA / Pod Identity / env / profile); optional `profile` and `role_arn` for local dev and cross-account AssumeRole. 76 - **`random`** — test-only provider that fabricates assessments within valid ranges. Use for local dev and integration tests; emits a startup warning so it doesn't silently ship to prod. Accepts an optional `seed` for deterministic runs. 77 78 ## Install 79 80 ```sh 81 go mod tidy 82 go build -o televibe ./cmd/televibe 83 ``` 84 85 ## Configure 86 87 Copy `televibe.toml.example` to `/etc/televibe/televibe.toml` and fill in: 88 89 - `[teleport]` — proxy address + path to an identity file for a Teleport user with permission to watch access requests and submit reviews. 90 - `[ai]` — pick a provider and supply its credentials. 91 - `[jira]` — API user, token, ITSM project key, and the status names to treat as approved/rejected (e.g. `"Approved"` / `"Rejected"`). 92 - `[risk]` — threshold, CUSTX pattern (defaults to `CUSTX-\d+`), off-hours window, timezone. 93 94 ### Environment variable overrides 95 96 Every scalar TOML key can be overridden by an environment variable. Use this to keep secrets out of the TOML file (e.g. Jira API tokens, Anthropic keys), or to vary deploy-specific values per environment. 97 98 **Naming rule:** `TV_` + the TOML section name + `_` + the field's TOML key, all uppercased. Nested sections (like `ai.anthropic`) concatenate with `_`. So `ai.anthropic.api_key` becomes `TV_AI_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. 99 100 **Precedence:** env var > `televibe.toml` > built-in default. 101 102 **Supported types:** `string`, `bool`, integer, float, and `time.Duration` (Go duration strings — `30s`, `2m`, `1h30m`). 103 104 **Not supported:** maps (`risk.escalation_thresholds`) and slices — TOML-only. 105 106 Common examples: 107 108 | Env var | Overrides | 109 | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | 110 | `TV_TELEPORT_ADDR` | `teleport.addr` | 111 | `TV_TELEPORT_IDENTITY_FILE` | `teleport.identity_file` | 112 | `TV_AI_PROVIDER` | `ai.provider` | 113 | `TV_AI_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `ai.anthropic.api_key` | 114 | `TV_AI_ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | `ai.anthropic.model` | 115 | `TV_AI_BEDROCK_REGION` | `ai.bedrock.region` | 116 | `TV_AI_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` | `ai.bedrock.model_id` | 117 | `TV_AI_BEDROCK_PROFILE` | `ai.bedrock.profile` | 118 | `TV_AI_BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN` | `ai.bedrock.role_arn` | 119 | `TV_JIRA_URL` | `jira.url` | 120 | `TV_JIRA_USERNAME` | `jira.username` | 121 | `TV_JIRA_API_TOKEN` | `jira.api_token` | 122 | `TV_JIRA_PROJECT` | `jira.project` | 123 | `TV_JIRA_POLL_INTERVAL` | `jira.poll_interval` (Go duration, e.g. `2m`) | 124 | `TV_RISK_TICKET_THRESHOLD` | `risk.ticket_threshold` | 125 | `TV_RISK_ESCALATION_ANNOTATION` | `risk.escalation_annotation` | 126 | `TV_RISK_ESCALATION_THRESHOLD` | `risk.escalation_threshold` | 127 | `TV_REPUTATION_PERSIST_PATH` | `reputation.persist_path` | 128 | `TV_REPUTATION_STARTING_SCORE` | `reputation.starting_score` | 129 | `TV_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` | `telemetry.enabled` | 130 | `TV_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT` | `telemetry.endpoint` | 131 | `TV_TELEMETRY_EXPORT_PERIOD` | `telemetry.export_period` (duration) | 132 | `TV_TELEMETRY_SHUTDOWN_GRACE` | `telemetry.shutdown_grace` (duration; `0s` disables the wait) | 133 | `TV_LOG_LEVEL` | `log.level` | 134 135 An invalid value (e.g. `TV_RISK_TICKET_THRESHOLD=abc`) fails startup with the offending variable name in the error, so misconfigurations surface immediately. 136 137 ### Teleport role 138 139 The plugin user needs a role roughly like: 140 141 ```yaml 142 kind: role 143 version: v7 144 metadata: 145 name: televibe-plugin 146 spec: 147 allow: 148 rules: 149 - resources: [access_request] 150 verbs: [list, read, update] 151 - resources: [access_plugin_data] 152 verbs: [update] 153 ``` 154 155 Issue an identity file with `tctl auth sign --user=televibe --out=/var/lib/teleport/televibe.pem --ttl=8760h --format=file`. 156 157 ### Jira workflow 158 159 The ITSM project needs statuses matching `jira.approved_status` and `jira.rejected_status`. When an SRE transitions the ticket to either, the poller reflects that decision back to the Teleport request on its next tick (`jira.poll_interval`, default `30s`). 160 161 ## Run 162 163 ```sh 164 ./televibe --config /etc/televibe/televibe.toml 165 ``` 166 167 JSON logs to stderr, level from `[log].level`. 168 169 ## Layout 170 171 ``` 172 televibe/ 173 ├── cmd/televibe/main.go entry point 174 ├── config.go TOML loader + validation 175 ├── app.go watcher loop + ITSM poller 176 ├── ai/ Provider interface, Anthropic / Bedrock / random impls 177 ├── risk/ scorer, tier table 178 ├── jira/itsm.go ticket create, status poll, restart rehydrate via JQL 179 ├── reputation/ per-user score store, JSON-file persistence 180 ├── telemetry/ OTLP meter provider, observable reputation gauge 181 └── televibe.toml.example 182 ``` 183 184 ## Restart safety 185 186 On startup, `televibe` runs a JQL search for open tickets labelled `teleport` in the ITSM project and pulls the Teleport request ID out of each ticket description to rebuild the held-request map. Risk tiers: | Score | Tier | Action | | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------- | | 0–24 | low | auto-approve, no Jira ticket | | 25–49 | medium | file ITSM ticket, hold request pending | | 50–74 | high | file ITSM ticket with tier label | | 75–100 | critical | file ITSM ticket with tier label | The ticket-creation threshold is configurable (`risk.ticket_threshold`). Session escalations — access requests carrying the `televibe.escalation` Teleport annotation — use a tighter fallback threshold (`risk.escalation_threshold`) and support per-role overrides in `risk.escalation_thresholds`. ## How it works ``` Teleport ──► watcher ──► scorer ──► AI provider ──► tier │ ├── below threshold ──► auto-approve via AccessReview │ └── at/above threshold ──► Jira ITSM ticket ──► poll status │ SRE approves/rejects │ ▼ Teleport AccessReview ``` **Risk components:** - **Structural (deterministic):** missing `CUSTX-###` ticket reference (+30), thin description `<40` chars (+15), off-hours request (+10). - **AI-judged (clamped):** description quality 0–25, privilege concern 0–25, anomalies 0–10. ## User reputation Every requester starts at `reputation.starting_score` (default `100`) and accumulates deductions for each bad request they file. Penalties and the `[floor, ceiling]` clamp are fully configurable: | Signal | Config key | Default | | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------- | | Missing CUSTX ticket | `reputation.penalty_missing_custx` | `10` | | Thin (<40 char) reason | `reputation.penalty_thin_description` | `5` | State is persisted as a JSON map at `reputation.persist_path` via atomic rename — no external database required. The file survives restarts; leave `persist_path` empty to keep everything in memory. Reputation only ever goes down. If somebody wants their number back, they can file better requests next quarter. Or not. ## Telemetry / shaming pipeline When `telemetry.enabled = true`, televibe stands up an OpenTelemetry `MeterProvider` with an OTLP/gRPC exporter pointed at the configured collector. It registers one observable gauge: - `televibe.user.reputation` — int64, tagged with `user`, observed every `telemetry.export_period` (default `15s`). Route your collector's output to Datadog (or Prometheus, or wherever) and the gauge lands tagged per user, ready to be pinned to a dashboard for the monthly team meeting. ## AI providers Pick one via `ai.provider`: - **`anthropic`** — direct call to the Anthropic Messages API. System prompt is sent with `cache_control: ephemeral` so repeated scoring hits the prompt cache. - **`bedrock`** — `bedrockruntime:InvokeModel` against a Claude-on-Bedrock model. Uses the default AWS credential chain (IRSA / Pod Identity / env / profile); optional `profile` and `role_arn` for local dev and cross-account AssumeRole. - **`random`** — test-only provider that fabricates assessments within valid ranges. Use for local dev and integration tests; emits a startup warning so it doesn't silently ship to prod. Accepts an optional `seed` for deterministic runs. ## Install ```sh go mod tidy go build -o televibe ./cmd/televibe ``` ## Configure Copy `televibe.toml.example` to `/etc/televibe/televibe.toml` and fill in: - `[teleport]` — proxy address + path to an identity file for a Teleport user with permission to watch access requests and submit reviews. - `[ai]` — pick a provider and supply its credentials. - `[jira]` — API user, token, ITSM project key, and the status names to treat as approved/rejected (e.g. `"Approved"` / `"Rejected"`). - `[risk]` — threshold, CUSTX pattern (defaults to `CUSTX-\d+`), off-hours window, timezone. ### Environment variable overrides Every scalar TOML key can be overridden by an environment variable. Use this to keep secrets out of the TOML file (e.g. Jira API tokens, Anthropic keys), or to vary deploy-specific values per environment. **Naming rule:** `TV_` + the TOML section name + `_` + the field's TOML key, all uppercased. Nested sections (like `ai.anthropic`) concatenate with `_`. So `ai.anthropic.api_key` becomes `TV_AI_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. **Precedence:** env var > `televibe.toml` > built-in default. **Supported types:** `string`, `bool`, integer, float, and `time.Duration` (Go duration strings — `30s`, `2m`, `1h30m`). **Not supported:** maps (`risk.escalation_thresholds`) and slices — TOML-only. Risk tiers: | Score | Tier | Action | | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------- | | 0–24 | low | auto-approve, no Jira ticket | | 25–49 | medium | file ITSM ticket, hold request pending | | 50–74 | high | file ITSM ticket with tier label | | 75–100 | critical | file ITSM ticket with tier label | The ticket-creation threshold is configurable (`risk.ticket_threshold`). Session escalations — access requests carrying the `televibe.escalation` Teleport annotation — use a tighter fallback threshold (`risk.escalation_threshold`) and support per-role overrides in `risk.escalation_thresholds`. ## How it works ``` Teleport ──► watcher ──► scorer ──► AI provider ──► tier │ ├── below threshold ──► auto-approve via AccessReview │ └── at/above threshold ──► Jira ITSM ticket ──► poll status │ SRE approves/rejects │ ▼ Teleport AccessReview ``` **Risk components:** - **Structural (deterministic):** missing `CUSTX-###` ticket reference (+30), thin description `<40` chars (+15), off-hours request (+10). - **AI-judged (clamped):** description quality 0–25, privilege concern 0–25, anomalies 0–10. ## User reputation Every requester starts at `reputation.starting_score` (default `100`) and accumulates deductions for each bad request they file. Penalties and the `[floor, ceiling]` clamp are fully configurable: | Signal | Config key | Default | | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------- | | Missing CUSTX ticket | `reputation.penalty_missing_custx` | `10` | | Thin (<40 char) reason | `reputation.penalty_thin_description` | `5` | State is persisted as a JSON map at `reputation.persist_path` via atomic rename — no external database required. package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"flag"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"televibe"
)

func main() {
	configPath := flag.String("config", "televibe.toml", "Path to TOML configuration")
	flag.Parse()

	cfg, err := televibe.LoadConfig(*configPath)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Error("config load failed", "path", *configPath, "err", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	setupLogging(cfg.Log.Level)

	ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer cancel()

	app, err := televibe.NewApp(ctx, cfg)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Error("app init failed", "err", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	runErr := app.Run(ctx)

	shutdownCtx, cancelShutdown := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancelShutdown()
	if err := app.Close(shutdownCtx); err != nil {
		slog.Warn("shutdown error", "err", err)
	}

	if runErr != nil && !errors.Is(runErr, context.Canceled) {
		slog.Error("app exited with error", "err", runErr)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func setupLogging(level string) {
	var l slog.Level
	switch level {
	case "debug":
		l = slog.LevelDebug
	case "warn":
		l = slog.LevelWarn
	case "error":
		l = slog.LevelError
	default:
		l = slog.LevelInfo
	}
	h := slog.NewJSONHandler(os.Stderr, &slog.HandlerOptions{Level: l})
	slog.SetDefault(slog.New(h))
}

1	// submit is a tiny helper for the local test harness — fires a Teleport
2	// access request as a given user, so you can watch televibe score it.
3	//
4	// Usage:
5	//
6	//	go run ./cmd/submit --reason "plz"
7	//	go run ./cmd/submit --reason "CUSTX-1234 fix prod-api latency regression"
8	package main
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"flag"
13		"fmt"
14		"log"
15		"strings"
16		"time"

18		"github.com/google/uuid"
19		"github.com/gravitational/teleport/api/client"
20		"github.com/gravitational/teleport/api/types"
21	)
22	
23	func main() {
24		addr := flag.String("addr", "localhost:3025", "teleport proxy address")
25		identity := flag.String("identity", "./local/identity/charles.pem", "identity file")
26		user := flag.String("user", "charles", "requesting user")
27		roles := flag.String("roles", "privileged", "comma-separated roles to request")
28		reason := flag.String("reason", "", "request reason")
29		flag.Parse()
30	
31		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
32		defer cancel()
33	
34		c, err := client.New(ctx, client.Config{
35			Addrs:                    []string{*addr},
36			Credentials:              []client.Credentials{client.LoadIdentityFile(*identity)},
37			InsecureAddressDiscovery: true,
38		})
39		if err != nil {
40			log.Fatalf("connect: %v", err)
41		}
42		defer c.Close()
43	
44		roleList := strings.Split(*roles, ",")
45		req, err := types.NewAccessRequest(uuid.NewString(), *user, roleList...)
46		if err != nil {
47			log.Fatalf("new access request: %v", err)
48		}
49		req.SetRequestReason(*reason)
50	
51		created, err := c.CreateAccessRequestV2(ctx, req)
52		if err != nil {
53			log.Fatalf("create access request: %v", err)
54		}
55		fmt.Printf("submitted request %s — user=%s roles=%v reason=%q\n",
56			created.GetName(), *user, roleList, *reason)
57	}

package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"flag"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"televibe"
)

func main() {
	configPath := flag.String("config", "televibe.toml", "Path to TOML configuration")
	flag.Parse()

	cfg, err := televibe.LoadConfig(*configPath)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Error("config load failed", "path", *configPath, "err", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	setupLogging(cfg.Log.Level)

	ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer cancel()

	app, err := televibe.NewApp(ctx, cfg)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Error("app init failed", "err", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	runErr := app.Run(ctx)

	shutdownCtx, cancelShutdown := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancelShutdown()
	if err := app.Close(shutdownCtx); err != nil {
		slog.Warn("shutdown error", "err", err)
	}

	if runErr != nil && !errors.Is(runErr, context.Canceled) {
		slog.Error("app exited with error", "err", runErr)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func setupLogging(level string) {
	var l slog.Level
	switch level {
	case "debug":
		l = slog.LevelDebug
	case "warn":
		l = slog.LevelWarn
	case "error":
		l = slog.LevelError
	default:
		l = slog.LevelInfo
	}
	h := slog.NewJSONHandler(os.Stderr, &slog.HandlerOptions{Level: l})
	slog.SetDefault(slog.New(h))
}

1	# Local test harness
2	
3	A docker-compose stack for exercising televibe end-to-end without real
4	Teleport, Anthropic, or Jira credentials.
5	
6	## What runs where
7	
8	| Component      | Where  | Notes                                                                    |
9	| -------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
10	| Teleport       | docker | Single-node auth+proxy cluster, self-signed TLS, port `3080`             |
11	| OTel collector | docker | OTLP/gRPC on `4317`, prints metrics to stdout via the debug exporter     |
12	| AI scoring     | inproc | `random` provider in `local/televibe.toml` fabricates assessments        |
13	| televibe       | host   | `go run ./cmd/televibe --config local/televibe.toml`                     |
14	| submit         | host   | `go run ./cmd/submit --reason "…"` fires test access requests            |
15	
16	Jira is stubbed: `risk.ticket_threshold` is cranked to `101` in
17	`local/televibe.toml`, so nothing ever hits Jira. Reputation scoring runs
18	before that branch, so the test loop is intact.
19	
20	## One-time setup
21	
22	```sh
23	# from apps/televibe
24	./local/bootstrap.sh
25	```
26	
27	This brings the stack up, applies the roles + users from
28	`local/resources.yaml`, and writes identity files to `local/identity/` for
29	the `televibe` plugin user and the `charles` test requester. Identities
30	are TTL 24h — re-run the script when they expire.
31

Session escalations — access requests carrying the `televibe.escalation` Teleport annotation — use a tighter fallback threshold (`risk.escalation_threshold`) and support per-role overrides in `risk.escalation_thresholds`. 19 20 ## How it works 21 22 ``` 23 Teleport ──► watcher ──► scorer ──► AI provider ──► tier 24 │ 25 ├── below threshold ──► auto-approve via AccessReview 26 │ 27 └── at/above threshold ──► Jira ITSM ticket ──► poll status 28 │ 29 SRE approves/rejects │ 30 ▼ 31 Teleport AccessReview 32 ``` 33 34 **Risk components:** 35 36 - **Structural (deterministic):** missing `CUSTX-###` ticket reference (+30), thin description `<40` chars (+15), off-hours request (+10). 37 - **AI-judged (clamped):** description quality 0–25, privilege concern 0–25, anomalies 0–10. 38 39 ## User reputation 40 41 Every requester starts at `reputation.starting_score` (default `100`) and 42 accumulates deductions for each bad request they file. Penalties and the 43 `[floor, ceiling]` clamp are fully configurable: 44 45 | Signal | Config key | Default | 46 | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------- | 47 | Missing CUSTX ticket | `reputation.penalty_missing_custx` | `10` | 48 | Thin (<40 char) reason | `reputation.penalty_thin_description` | `5` | 49 50 State is persisted as a JSON map at `reputation.persist_path` via atomic 51 rename — no external database required. The file survives restarts; leave 52 `persist_path` empty to keep everything in memory. 53 54 Reputation only ever goes down. If somebody wants their number back, 55 they can file better requests next quarter. Or not. 56 57 ## Telemetry / shaming pipeline 58 59 When `telemetry.enabled = true`, televibe stands up an OpenTelemetry 60 `MeterProvider` with an OTLP/gRPC exporter pointed at the configured 61 collector. System prompt is sent with `cache_control: ephemeral` so repeated scoring hits the prompt cache. 75 - **`bedrock`** — `bedrockruntime:InvokeModel` against a Claude-on-Bedrock model. Uses the default AWS credential chain (IRSA / Pod Identity / env / profile); optional `profile` and `role_arn` for local dev and cross-account AssumeRole. 76 - **`random`** — test-only provider that fabricates assessments within valid ranges. Use for local dev and integration tests; emits a startup warning so it doesn't silently ship to prod. Accepts an optional `seed` for deterministic runs. 77 78 ## Install 79 80 ```sh 81 go mod tidy 82 go build -o televibe ./cmd/televibe 83 ``` 84 85 ## Configure 86 87 Copy `televibe.toml.example` to `/etc/televibe/televibe.toml` and fill in: 88 89 - `[teleport]` — proxy address + path to an identity file for a Teleport user with permission to watch access requests and submit reviews. 90 - `[ai]` — pick a provider and supply its credentials. 91 - `[jira]` — API user, token, ITSM project key, and the status names to treat as approved/rejected (e.g. `"Approved"` / `"Rejected"`). 92 - `[risk]` — threshold, CUSTX pattern (defaults to `CUSTX-\d+`), off-hours window, timezone. 93 94 ### Dry-run mode 95 96 Set `dry_run = true` (or `TV_DRY_RUN=true`) to score every incoming request and 97 log the decision televibe *would* make — auto-approve, or "would file ITSM 98 ticket and hold pending" — without actually calling Teleport or Jira. `0s` disables the wait) | 142 | `TV_LOG_LEVEL` | `log.level` | 143 144 An invalid value (e.g. `TV_RISK_TICKET_THRESHOLD=abc`) fails startup with the offending variable name in the error, so misconfigurations surface immediately. 145 146 ### Teleport role 147 148 The plugin user needs a role roughly like: 149 150 ```yaml 151 kind: role 152 version: v7 153 metadata: 154 name: televibe-plugin 155 spec: 156 allow: 157 rules: 158 - resources: [access_request] 159 verbs: [list, read, update] 160 - resources: [access_plugin_data] 161 verbs: [update] 162 ``` 163 164 Issue an identity file with `tctl auth sign --user=televibe --out=/var/lib/teleport/televibe.pem --ttl=8760h --format=file`. 165 166 ### Jira workflow 167 168 The ITSM project needs statuses matching `jira.approved_status` and `jira.rejected_status`. Restarts don't duplicate tickets. 196 197 ## License 198 199 TBD. 200

# ruth — Teleport access plugin with AI risk scoring
# Copy to /etc/ruth/ruth.toml and fill in.
#
# Any scalar key can also be overridden via a RUTH_-prefixed environment

# new threshold or AI provider before flipping the switch in prod.
# dry_run = false

[teleport]
addr = "proxy.example.com:443"
identity_file = "/var/lib/teleport/ruth.pem"

[ai]
# Exactly one of: "anthropic", "bedrock", "random".

# Authentication: by default the AWS SDK default credential chain is used,

# env vars, and ~/.aws/credentials — no config needed in prod.
# profile = "dev"                           # named shared-config profile (local dev)

rejected_status = "Rejected"

# Off-hours window applies a +10 risk bump. Wraps midnight when start > end.
